newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CSFB sees Swiss franc down vs mark, SNB stays easy.
newsitem.headline: CSFB sees Swiss franc down vs mark, SNB stays easy.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston said it expected the Swiss franc to resume its drop against the mark after a correction triggered in part by analysts' mistaken belief the Swiss National Bank was tightening monetary policy.

"Today mark/Swiss should finish its brief correction and resume the uptrend," CSFB said in a trading strategy bulletin. "Mark/Swiss will begin to rise very soon and successfully attack the 87.30/40 resistance zone," it said.

CSFB said the mark's fall yesterday reflected markets' misinterpretation of the SNB's announcement it expected M0 money supply to grow 0.1 percent in the first quarter or an annualised 0.4 percent against the the fourth-quarter 1996 base.

"This announcement does certainly not reflect any tightening intentions," it said. "On the contrary, the SNB confirmed that this year base money growth should again exceed the five-year one percent target path.

"In order to achieve that, monetary policy will have to remain expansionary for quite some time. Given the bleak outlook for the economy, monetary policy will have to be eased again. Both short- and long-term Swiss interest rates will drop sharply in the coming month, leading to much higher levels in mark/Swiss."

It attributed the projected drop in first-quarter money supply growth rates to the fact that Swiss tend to hoard banknotes in the fourth quarter to meeet tax payments. This typically reverses in the first quarter.
"Thus the strong base money growth in Q4 and the expected subsequent drop mainly reflects this seasonal pattern of bank note holdings," it said.
